--- title: "How did the first flight compare?" --- The first flight of the corrected glider, filmed and measured, against what this chapter predicted for it. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Specified **Flight video `IMG_1665.mov`** · filmed by the user, 2026-08-31 · the glider as flown carries the euro 50 cent, not the 1p. Read off the video: it decodes at 640 × 360 and 30 fps; the glider leaves the hand at frame 100 and is lying still on the grass by frame 156; its wingspan measures 20 px across when at rest, read off a 12× crop with a 5 px rule. ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Assumed The camera's **horizontal field of view is 66°**, typical of a phone's main lens, which is what converts pixels to metres — nothing in the video states it. The glider is assumed to **lie broadside** at rest, so its measured span is not foreshortened; the fuselage is visibly shorter than the span in those frames even though it is longer in fact, which is what a fuselage pointing away from the camera looks like. **Release height 1.5 m**, from the video: eye level, arm extended, level push. ::: ::: {#cc507a90 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} FPS, WIDTH_PX, HFOV = 30.0, 640, 66.0 F_RELEASE, F_DOWN = 100, 156 # last frame in hand / first frame at rest SPAN_PX, SPAN_ERR = 20.0, 2.0 # apparent span at rest, and its read error H_REL = 1.5 # m, release height # Pixels to metres: a span of S metres at range d subtends f*S/d pixels. f_px = (WIDTH_PX / 2) / np.tand(HFOV / 2) t_aloft = (F_DOWN - F_RELEASE) / FPS rng = f_px * b_proj / SPAN_PX rng_err = rng * SPAN_ERR / SPAN_PX # one pixel of read error, propagated v_avg = rng / t_aloft # The aircraft as flown: the 50 cent in place of the fitted 1p. m_flown = 0.016 - 3.56e-3 + 7.80e-3 x_flown = neutral_point() - 0.10 * c_w t = trim(m_flown, x_flown) a_stall, CL_max = stall(t["V"]) V_stall = (2 * m_flown * 9.81 / (1.225 * S_w * CL_max)) ** 0.5 rng_floor = V_stall * t_aloft # it cannot have flown slower than this rng_trim = t["V"] * t_aloft # what the model's own speed implies pred_rng, pred_t = t["LD"] * H_REL, H_REL / t["sink"] # The same airframe at the balance point it was built with, for contrast. Its # stall must be read at its own trim speed, not at the flown one. heavy = trim(0.016, x_flown + 0.015) heavy_past = heavy["alpha"] - stall(heavy["V"])[0] ``` ::: **Answer.** It flew as designed. The glider was airborne for 1\.87 s against a predicted 1\.92 s — agreement to 3% — and covered 7\.2 ± 0\.7 m against a predicted 8\.6 m. Time is the number to trust here: it is counted in frames and needs no camera calibration, whereas range rests on a 20-pixel measurement and an assumed lens. **It was not thrown.** @fig-flight shows a level push at eye height with the arm extending — the release the glide prediction assumes, not a hard overarm throw. That matters, because it is what makes the comparison fair; an earlier read of this same video as a hard throw was wrong, and the wide frames are what settle it. There is no zoom, no ballooning and no pitch oscillation after release, which is what an over-speed launch produces and which would be plainly visible. **On launch speed.** The video cannot measure it directly — the glider's attitude changes faster than its range does, so apparent span is unusable in the first half-second — but it is boxed in tightly from both sides. It cannot have left the hand below the stall speed of 4\.1 m/s or it would have dropped, and the absence of any phugoid rules out much above trim. **Launch was therefore at essentially the trim speed, 4\.5 m/s** — which is exactly what a level hand push should give, and why the flight settled immediately instead of hunting. **The one inconsistency, and what it means.** The measured range implies an average speed of 3\.9 m/s, which is *below* the 4\.1 m/s stall — physically impossible for 1\.87 s of steady flight. So the range is underestimated, not the model overestimated: flight time alone puts the floor at 7\.6 m, and the model's own trim speed over the measured time gives 8\.5 m, within 1% of the prediction. Two pixels of span at rest is all it takes; that is the measurement to improve, and a metre rule laid on the grass would remove the assumed lens entirely. The glide itself is clean (@fig-flight, third panel): wings level, dihedral holding, no wing drop, no mush. That is the corrected balance doing its job — the same aircraft at its as-built balance point was predicted to trim 0\.3° past the stall and to do none of those things. ::: {#cell-fig-flight .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.image as mpimg fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 1.3)) ax.imshow(mpimg.imread("chapters/02-mceagle-300/flight-2026-08-31.png")) ax.axis("off") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Four frames from the flight. The release is a level push at eye height, not a throw. Circles mark the glider where it is small: in the glide, and at rest on the grass.](2026-08-31-05-how-did-the-first-flight-compare_files/figure-html/fig-flight-output-1.png){#fig-flight width=954 height=180} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-flight .cell tbl-cap='Measured against predicted. Time aloft is counted in frames; range depends on the assumed lens and a 20-pixel span, and carries the uncertainty.' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "": ["time aloft", "range", "average speed", "launch speed", "trim speed", "stall speed"], "predicted": [f"{pred_t:.2f} s", f"{pred_rng:.1f} m", f"{t['V']:.1f} m/s", f"{t['V']:.1f} m/s", f"{t['V']:.2f} m/s", f"{V_stall:.2f} m/s"], "measured": [f"{t_aloft:.2f} s", f"{rng:.1f} ± {rng_err:.1f} m", f"{v_avg:.1f} m/s", "not directly measurable", "—", "—"], "note": ["frames counted, no calibration needed", f"floor of {rng_floor:.1f} m from time and stall speed", "below stall, so the range is low", "bounded to trim by stall and by no phugoid", "model, at the flown mass and balance", "model, at CL max"], }).style.hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

range 8.6 m 7.2 ± 0.7 m floor of 7.6 m from time and stall speed
average speed 4.5 m/s 3.9 m/s below stall, so the range is low

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def trim(mass, x_cg, V=5.0, alpha=None, iters=60): """ The angle of attack and speed at which an aircraft of this mass and balance flies itself: pitching moment about the CG zero, lift equal to weight. Takes mass and CG rather than a MassProperties, so it works for a glider that has been built and weighed as readily as for one that has been summed. AeroBuildup reports Cm about `xyz_ref`, so it is shifted to the CG first: Cm_cg = Cm_ref + CL * (x_cg - x_ref) / c_ref. Iterated rather than solved, because CL and V each determine the other and the speed moves the polar through Reynolds number. `slope` is dCm/dalpha at the crossing -- negative is a restoring moment. That is the honest stability test: it needs no neutral point, so it does not inherit the ambiguity in defining one. """ a = np.linspace(-2, 14, 161) if alpha is None else alpha for _ in range(iters): p = polars(a, V=V) Cm_cg = np.array(p["Cm"]) + np.array(p["CL"]) * (x_cg - x_qc_w) / c_w i = int(np.argmin(abs(Cm_cg))) V = (2 * mass * 9.81 / (1.225 * S_w * float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]))) ** 0.5 CL, CD = float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]), float(np.array(p["CD"])[i]) return dict(alpha=a[i], V=V, CL=CL, CD=CD, LD=CL / CD, slope=(Cm_cg[i + 1] - Cm_cg[i - 1]) / (a[i + 1] - a[i - 1]), Re=p["Re_c"], sink=V / (1 + (CL / CD) ** 2) ** 0.5) def stall(V, alpha=None): """ Angle of attack where lift first stops rising, and the CL there. The FIRST peak, deliberately, not the global maximum. NeuralFoil's curve turns over near 10 degrees, dips, and then climbs again well past 20 -- deep post-stall behaviour the model is not meant to represent. A global argmax picks that second branch at some speeds and reports a stall angle of 16-24 degrees, which is nonsense for this wing. """ a = np.linspace(0, 24, 241) if alpha is None else alpha CL = np.array(polars(a, V=V)["CL"]) for i in range(1, len(a) - 1): if CL[i] >= CL[i - 1] and CL[i] > CL[i + 1]: return a[i], float(CL[i]) return a[int(np.argmax(CL))], float(CL.max()) ``` :::
